extraction.Name: Leroy Cuny
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to his 160 acre allotment; but he was advised by the Indian Agency that it was reported to the tax collector, and he would have taxes to pay, or would finally lose it, so he accepted it
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold it to Charles Cuny, receiving $300.00 in cash, 12 head of horses, valued at $50.00 each, also, Charles Cuny paid these back taxes; and Leroy Cuny gave Charles Cuny a deed to his land
extraction.Buyer: Charles Cuny; $300.00 in cash, 12 head of horses valued at $50.00 each, plus payment of back taxes
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: in 1920, being behind in taxes, he sold it to Charles Cuny; he does not consider it a fair price for his land, but took it because the taxes were unpaid, and he could not pay them
extraction.Occupation/Income: works out on farms for a living
extraction.NOTES: Mentally competent, has pretty good health; has been married but his wife is dead; has three minor children to support; finds it hard to make ends meet; has never received any aid from the County, State or United States Government; document sworn November 21, 1928 | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Shannon County, South Dakota (Pine Ridge area)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')
